**Telemetry scope — VM experience as observed by the hypervisor:** VM disk/network counters differ from Ceph/RBD, physical-device, NIC or switch measurements; the views are complementary. Fleet panels use Hypervisor only. Selected-scope views also use the Project/Instance filters shown above.

panels.description:
Scope: fleet panels use all VM observations on the selected Hypervisor targets. Project, name and Instance filters can be carried in links even though their controls are hidden here. They narrow the selected-scope snapshots, inventory, latency, mining, retype and resource-freshness views; the banner shows them and Reset scope clears them.

Graphs cover the selected time range; snapshots use its end. VM-side disk and network counters describe the experience observed through Libvirt/QEMU, not physical disks, Ceph/RBD pools, host NICs or the network fabric. Use backend telemetry to explain infrastructure causes. Configured allocation can retain the last observed dimensions.

Viewing: legends start with the highest Max. Last is the right-edge value and remains unavailable for ended series; Max is the highest plotted sample. Scroll legends and tables, click column headings to sort, and click a legend name to isolate a series. All matching table rows are returned. Names are display metadata; links retain UUID identity, including duplicate names. Full identifiers are available in Inspect → Data with field overrides disabled. Bytes and bits use automatic IEC prefixes. Line colours identify measurements; host conntrack utilization alone uses fixed capacity bands. Missing or stale observations are not healthy zero activity. Check source coverage when a value or table is empty.

The guest estimate is Libvirt balloon current minus balloon usable, where usable corresponds to guest MemAvailable; it is not QEMU RSS. Host used is total minus available.

Guest/host ratios are diagnostic comparisons, not physical RAM uniquely occupied by VMs; they may exceed 100%. They exclude QEMU overhead and can include shared guest pages. The configured-allocation denominator is preserved. Missing guest-used measurements or an unhealthy source omit the affected aggregate instead of treating missing memory as zero.

panels.title: Configured block devices
VM disk latency and observation coverage
panels.description:
One row per observed storage source in the selected project/instance scope at the range end. Read/write/flush latency is five-minute total operation time / total completed operations from running VMs on usable targets, not a percentile or physical-drive measurement.

No read/write/flush I/O in 5m means usable counter pairs but no completed operations. Unavailable means timing evidence is missing, invalid, stale or unhealthy. Read/Write/Flush measured columns count attachments with usable paired counters, including idle disks. Read + write IOPS needs both request counters but not timing counters.

The Observed devices column counts runtime block-device observations on VMs last observed running, including retained observations on unhealthy targets. It is not a physical-disk count or a count restricted to configured disk attachments. Compare measured counts with observed devices and usable targets with selected targets; missing inventory can still hide devices. Unclassified source means the runtime device could not be matched to a recognised source; use the Instance disk-source table to inspect it.
